title: Circular Uses Report (cycles + fix plan)
summary: Finds uses cycles among indexed units and, on request, proposes a followable refactoring plan to break them
intro: Read this when the compiler complains about circular references or a project dependency graph feels tangled. It finds uses cycles among indexed units (--f2047 narrows to the interface-only ones dcc rejects) and, on request, writes a refactoring playbook per group: what moves, the uses edits, the new-unit text and the predicted result, plus the exact cycles --fix commands that make the mechanical part for you. Where the playbook cannot cut a cycle it says so per edge and names the reason.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Circular Uses Report (cycles + fix plan)...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Circular Uses Report (cycles + fix plan)...
Ask for the plan to get the refactoring playbook that breaks them

surfaces.usage: drag-lint cycles --db <file.sqlite> [--edges] [--causes] [--plan [--project <X.dproj>]] [--f2047 [--unit <stem>]] [--fix --project <X.dproj> [--cycle <n> | --unit <stem>] [--part a|b|all] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-reindex] [--no-compile] [--shadow-out <dir>] [--rsvars <path>] [--build-timeout <s>]] [--format json|text] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--platform win32|win64] [--rules-dir <dir>] (circular unit deps; --f2047 = only the interface-only cycles dcc rejects with F2047, each edge with its forcing symbols and the next --plan / --fix commands; --plan = mechanical refactoring playbook: moves, uses edits, new-unit text, checklist + predicted output, and a "Fix it" block per group naming the exact --fix dry-run and --apply commands; --fix = the mechanical fix of one group, see the cycles-fix entry)
help: drag-lint cycles             --db <file.sqlite>    [--edges] [--causes] [--plan [--project <X.dproj>]] [--f2047 [--unit <stem>]] [--fix --project <X.dproj> [--cycle <n> | --unit <stem>] [--part a|b|all] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-reindex] [--no-compile] [--shadow-out <dir>] [--rsvars <path>] [--build-timeout <s>]] [--format json|text] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--platform win32|win64] [--rules-dir <dir>]   (circular unit deps; --f2047 = only the interface-only cycles dcc rejects with F2047: units, each interface edge with the symbols forcing it, and the next --plan / --fix commands; --unit <stem> (the name in dcc's message) narrows it, a unit in no such cycle is exit 0 with a note; --format json = [{units[],edges[{from,to,symbols[]}],plan,fix}]; --fix = the mechanical cycle fix for ONE group (the first mechanical one, or --cycle / --unit; text names the groups it did not plan): dry run = verdict + cycle-fix/1 JSON, no source written, stages the result in a shadow tree (default C:\TEMP\draglint_cyclefix_<pid>\, deleted at exit unless a message of the run cites a file in it, then kept and named on stderr; --shadow-out names another, never deleted) and builds the project (msbuild /p:Config=Debug for --platform, default win64) unless --no-compile, exit 0 mechanical / 1 refused / 2 error; --apply writes it (.BCK<n> backups unless --no-backup), builds, re-indexes unless --no-reindex and re-runs cycles against the prediction, exit 0 written and verified (or written with --no-reindex, unverified) / 1 refused, rolled back after a compile error or build timeout, or written but not verified / 2 error: a write or build failed part-way (rolled back, project not changed, or the rollback failure is named) or bad flags; a rollback restores the sources, not the DCUs the failed build wrote: rebuild after a rollback; --apply --no-compile is exit 2; --rsvars <path> = the Studio build environment the compile gate calls (default: the Studio the registry or BDS names; forwarded to every --part all iteration; a missing file is exit 2); --build-timeout <s> = whole seconds one build may take (default 0 = no limit; forwarded to every --part all iteration; anything but a whole number >= 0 is exit 2); a stand-down request (drag-lint shutdown --db <db>, or the IDE's Cancel) kills the build, rolls an --apply back and exits 1 ("cancelled -- rolled back"); --part all needs --apply, refuses --no-reindex; --plan = mechanical refactoring playbook: moves, uses edits, new-unit text, checklist + predicted output, and a "Fix it" block per group (the exact --fix dry-run and --apply commands; --project names the project in them, else <your.dproj>); --library-db / --platform name the platform library --plan reads class ancestry from (default: the manifest's library for win64; --library-db none = no library); --rules-dir is forwarded to every --part all iteration; --format json --causes adds per-group fix{available,part,dry_run,apply,edges[],reason,followup} and edges[] with each edge's surface: members read, writes, construction, class methods, routine + signature types)
